newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares extend fall, rebound seen Wednesday.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares extend fall, rebound seen Wednesday.

text.p: Polish shares fell for the third session running and analysts said that, after a likely rebound on Wednesday, investors would be watching for more data on the current flooding and fall of the domestic currency.

"Factors outside the bourse such as interest rates, foreign currencies which are going up so quickly and inflation pressure...makes the bourse very dangerous," said Jan Koch, a trader at Polish Development Bank (PBR) brokerage.
Poland's coalition cabinet was meeting on Tuesday to decide proposals for changes to the 1997 budget and other laws due to the flooding.
Foreign currency markets were jittery over any possible impact on Poland's swollen budget deficit and the zloty slid nearly five percent.

Also on Tuesday a central bank deputy head would give no comment on a potential increase of interest rates though a week ago the bank said it might need to increase market rates to control its operational target of reserve money growth.
The main market's all-share WIG index fell 2.3 percent to 15,107.7 points and turnover fell 8.4 percent to 197.9 million zlotys on both markets.
Analysts said the steepness of this week's falls meant that at least a partial recovery was likely.
KGHM fell 9.7 percent in profit-taking in heavy trade to 19.5 zlotys but analysts said the copper company's stock could rebound on Wednesday and then stabilise.
They said Polifarb Cieszyn's 8.2-percent drop might have been due to its stated need to repair flood damage.
NFI units fell 8.6 percent on flood concerns but analysts saw a rebound on Wednesday. The NIF index, down 2.2 percent, had fallen 8.6 percent on Monday.
